Explore liberally before deciding. Use the tools whenever they can test a route, target, threat, rule, memory, or assumption. Do not avoid a useful tool call merely to save tokens. The available tools have these purposes:

check_neighbours looks up an area's direct neighbours and their current owners, units, wounds, orders, terrain and castles. Ask about the battlefield when checking possible support. Direct neighbours are not the same as all legal ship-transport destinations.

reachable_areas finds geographic movement routes from any area, even empty or enemy-held, using your current ships for transport. It returns routes and transport ships, not legal unit groups. Armies, orders, Supply, combat strength and port control do not filter the results; use actionGuidance for legality.

inspect_house_card returns the exact printed strength, combat icons and ability text for one House card in this game, plus whether it is currently available. Use it when card text could change a combat calculation.

recall_game_state retrieves an earlier observation from your private game history. Use it when a past decision matters; the current observation takes precedence if facts differ.

remember_strategy records a proposed update to your private plan. It does not place orders or move units, and the note is saved only after your final action is accepted.

ask_rules_oracle asks a rules specialist a focused question using the local rulebook and FAQ. It explains rules; it does not choose or submit your action.

These tools do not submit a gameplay action. After a tool returns, inspect its result and follow up wherever uncertainty remains. Use multiple calls when they test different targets, threats, rules, or memories. Treat tool results as evidence and revise your plan when they contradict an assumption. You are not limited to one tool call.

Explore as deeply as the decision warrants. Tool calls return evidence to this same run, so inspect each result and continue exploring when useful. When ready, you MUST call submit_action with arguments matching its current schema. That tool is the only way to submit the action and finish this decision. The harness checks it against the current game state before sending it to the server.

calls.output:
The “Wildlings‑Attack” Westeros card does **not** assign a fixed strength. When that card is drawn, a wildling attack is resolved using the Wildling Threat token that is on the Wildlings track.

**Rule** – Wildling attacks, page 22:  
> “1. Determine Wildling Strength: Check the current position of the Wildling Threat token. The number printed on its position on the Wildlings track is the strength of the wildling attack.”

Thus, after the *Wildlings‑Attack* card is drawn, the Night’s Watch must meet or exceed **the numeric value shown on the Wildling Threat token’s current space on the Wildlings track**. (The token’s position is set earlier in the Westeros Phase by advancing one space for each Wildling icon on the three Westeros cards drawn – see “Advance Wildlings Track” in the Game round and Westeros phase, page 7.) 

Because the actual token location depends on the game’s prior draws and icon advances, the exact strength cannot be stated without knowing the current board state. The rule requires checking the token’s printed number at that moment.

check_neighbours looks up an area's direct neighbours and their current owners, units, wounds, orders, terrain and castles. Ask about the battlefield when checking possible support. Direct neighbours are not the same as all legal ship-transport destinations.

reachable_areas finds geographic movement routes from any area, even empty or enemy-held, using your current ships for transport. It returns routes and transport ships, not legal unit groups. inspect_house_card returns the exact printed strength, combat icons and ability text for one House card in this game, plus whether it is currently available. Use it when card text could change a combat calculation.

recall_game_state retrieves an earlier observation from your private game history. Use it when a past decision matters; the current observation takes precedence if facts differ.

remember_strategy records a proposed update to your private plan. It does not place orders or move units, and the note is saved only after your final action is accepted.

ask_rules_oracle asks a rules specialist a focused question using the local rulebook and FAQ. It explains rules; it does not choose or submit your action.

These tools do not submit a gameplay action. After a tool returns, inspect its result and follow up wherever uncertainty remains. Use multiple calls when they test different targets, threats, rules, or memories. Treat tool results as evidence and revise your plan when they contradict an assumption. You are not limited to one tool call.

Explore as deeply as the decision warrants. Tool calls return evidence to this same run, so inspect each result and continue exploring when useful. You are playing House Baratheon in round 2. This is a new decision; you have not submitted an action for it.

You are placing planning orders for this round. Assign an order preference to each required occupied area, respecting the displayed restrictions and starred-order limit. submit_action submits the whole order draft and marks your house ready. These orders determine what your armies can do later; this decision does not move units. A single land unit can capture an empty castle with a March order. Defence and Support orders do not move that unit or claim neighbouring land. Consolidate Power in an open sea earns no power; a port follows the separate port rule. The harness allocates the physical order tokens, preserving higher-priority preferences when not all requested categories fit the available tokens. Priority 100 is most important; 0 is least important. Plan how to gain castle areas this round. Use Defence or Support when you have a concrete battle to protect or assist; otherwise these orders can leave an army unable to expand.

A castle and a stronghold each count as ONE controlled castle area for victory. The map's castle=2 denotes a stronghold's mustering capacity, not two victory points. Single units in separate areas do not count as armies against Supply; an army has two or more units.

Your home symbol keeps Dragonstone yours when your last unit leaves; no power token is needed.

Explore liberally before deciding. Use the tools whenever they can test a route, target, threat, rule, memory, or assumption. Do not avoid a useful tool call merely to save tokens. The available tools have these purposes:

check_neighbours looks up an area's direct neighbours and their current owners, units, wounds, orders, terrain and castles. Ask about the battlefield when checking possible support. Direct neighbours are not the same as all legal ship-transport destinations.

reachable_areas finds geographic movement routes from any area, even empty or enemy-held, using your current ships for transport. It returns routes and transport ships, not legal unit groups. Armies, orders, Supply, combat strength and port control do not filter the results; use actionGuidance for legality.

inspect_house_card returns the exact printed strength, combat icons and ability text for one House card in this game, plus whether it is currently available. Use it when card text could change a combat calculation.

recall_game_state retrieves an earlier observation from your private game history. Use it when a past decision matters; the current observation takes precedence if facts differ.

remember_strategy records a proposed update to your private plan. It does not place orders or move units, and the note is saved only after your final action is accepted.

ask_rules_oracle asks a rules specialist a focused question using the local rulebook and FAQ. It explains rules; it does not choose or submit your action.

These tools do not submit a gameplay action. After a tool returns, inspect its result and follow up wherever uncertainty remains. Use multiple calls when they test different targets, threats, rules, or memories. Treat tool results as evidence and revise your plan when they contradict an assumption. check_neighbours looks up an area's direct neighbours and their current owners, units, wounds, orders, terrain and castles. Ask about the battlefield when checking possible support. Direct neighbours are not the same as all legal ship-transport destinations.

reachable_areas finds geographic movement routes from any area, even empty or enemy-held, using your current ships for transport. It returns routes and transport ships, not legal unit groups. inspect_house_card returns the exact printed strength, combat icons and ability text for one House card in this game, plus whether it is currently available. Use it when card text could change a combat calculation.

recall_game_state retrieves an earlier observation from your private game history. Use it when a past decision matters; the current observation takes precedence if facts differ.

remember_strategy records a proposed update to your private plan. It does not place orders or move units, and the note is saved only after your final action is accepted.

ask_rules_oracle asks a rules specialist a focused question using the local rulebook and FAQ. It explains rules; it does not choose or submit your action.

recall_game_state retrieves an earlier observation from your private game history. Use it when a past decision matters; the current observation takes precedence if facts differ.

remember_strategy records a proposed update to your private plan. It does not place orders or move units, and the note is saved only after your final action is accepted.

ask_rules_oracle asks a rules specialist a focused question using the local rulebook and FAQ. It explains rules; it does not choose or submit your action.

check_neighbours looks up an area's direct neighbours and their current owners, units, wounds, orders, terrain and castles. Ask about the battlefield when checking possible support. Direct neighbours are not the same as all legal ship-transport destinations.

reachable_areas finds geographic movement routes from any area, even empty or enemy-held, using your current ships for transport. It returns routes and transport ships, not legal unit groups. recall_game_state retrieves an earlier observation from your private game history. Use it when a past decision matters; the current observation takes precedence if facts differ.

remember_strategy records a proposed update to your private plan. It does not place orders or move units, and the note is saved only after your final action is accepted.

ask_rules_oracle asks a rules specialist a focused question using the local rulebook and FAQ. It explains rules; it does not choose or submit your action.

These tools do not submit a gameplay action. After a tool returns, inspect its result and follow up wherever uncertainty remains. Use multiple calls when they test different targets, threats, rules, or memories. Treat tool results as evidence and revise your plan when they contradict an assumption. You are playing House Lannister in round 3. This is a new decision; you have not submitted an action for it.

inspect_top_wildling_card: Use this Messenger Raven opportunity to inspect the top Wildling card. This spends the decision; keeping or burying the revealed card is a subsequent decision.

skip_raven_order_replacement: Decline the Messenger Raven opportunity and keep the placed orders.

Explore liberally before deciding. Use the tools whenever they can test a route, target, threat, rule, memory, or assumption. Do not avoid a useful tool call merely to save tokens. The available tools have these purposes:

check_neighbours looks up an area's direct neighbours and their current owners, units, wounds, orders, terrain and castles. Ask about the battlefield when checking possible support. Direct neighbours are not the same as all legal ship-transport destinations.

reachable_areas finds geographic movement routes from any area, even empty or enemy-held, using your current ships for transport. It returns routes and transport ships, not legal unit groups. Armies, orders, Supply, combat strength and port control do not filter the results; use actionGuidance for legality.

inspect_house_card returns the exact printed strength, combat icons and ability text for one House card in this game, plus whether it is currently available. Use it when card text could change a combat calculation.

recall_game_state retrieves an earlier observation from your private game history. Use it when a past decision matters; the current observation takes precedence if facts differ.

remember_strategy records a proposed update to your private plan. It does not place orders or move units, and the note is saved only after your final action is accepted.

ask_rules_oracle asks a rules specialist a focused question using the local rulebook and FAQ. It explains rules; it does not choose or submit your action.

These tools do not submit a gameplay action. After a tool returns, inspect its result and follow up wherever uncertainty remains. Use multiple calls when they test different targets, threats, rules, or memories. Treat tool results as evidence and revise your plan when they contradict an assumption. You are not limited to one tool call.

Explore as deeply as the decision warrants. Tool calls return evidence to this same run, so inspect each result and continue exploring when useful. When ready, you MUST call submit_action with arguments matching its current schema. That tool is the only way to submit the action and finish this decision. The harness checks it against the current game state before sending it to the server.

decisionJournal: Round 1 place-orders: Priorities: Capture The Reach castle (or Crackclaw Point) using a starred March from Kingswood to secure a new castle area. Use a regular Consolidate Power at Shipbreaker Bay to gain an extra power token for future bidding. Assign a regular March at Dragonstone for flexibility to move the knight or footman later, possibly to reinforce The Reach or capture another target. Preserve control of key territories and stay within the single starred order limit.

Round 1 resolve-single-march: Moved footman from Dragonstone to capture Crackclaw Point, gaining a second castle while keeping the knight at Dragonstone. No power token needed. Next focus on resolving Kingswood march to secure The Reach or reinforce positions.

Round 1 resolve-single-march: Moved footman from Kingswood to The Reach, capturing a Castle (new Baratheon castle area). Used one power token to keep control of Kingswood after vacating. Follow-up: consolidate power at Shipbreaker Bay for extra power, and monitor Lannister and Stark actions.

Round 2 bidding: Bid 2 power tokens to help the Night's Watch meet the wildling strength while preserving most of our power for future bidding and mustering. This balances defense against the wildlings with maintaining resources for upcoming influence bids and expansion.

Round 2 place-orders: Capture Kings Landing castle using footman from The Reach (starred March for +1 combat). Support from Crackclaw Point to increase combat strength. Move knight from Dragonstone to Kingswood via ship transport for future staging. Consolidate Power at Shipbreaker Bay for extra power token for upcoming bids.

This maintains supply compliance and keeps our castle count while advancing towards a stronghold capture.
Round 2 resolve-single-march: Capture Blackwater to gain 2 supply icons, increase supply track, and retain control of The Reach castle with a power token.

Explore liberally before deciding. Use the tools whenever they can test a route, target, threat, rule, memory, or assumption. Do not avoid a useful tool call merely to save tokens. The available tools have these purposes:

check_neighbours looks up an area's direct neighbours and their current owners, units, wounds, orders, terrain and castles. Ask about the battlefield when checking possible support. Direct neighbours are not the same as all legal ship-transport destinations.

reachable_areas finds geographic movement routes from any area, even empty or enemy-held, using your current ships for transport. It returns routes and transport ships, not legal unit groups. Armies, orders, Supply, combat strength and port control do not filter the results; use actionGuidance for legality.

inspect_house_card returns the exact printed strength, combat icons and ability text for one House card in this game, plus whether it is currently available. Use it when card text could change a combat calculation.

recall_game_state retrieves an earlier observation from your private game history. Use it when a past decision matters; the current observation takes precedence if facts differ.

remember_strategy records a proposed update to your private plan. It does not place orders or move units, and the note is saved only after your final action is accepted.

ask_rules_oracle asks a rules specialist a focused question using the local rulebook and FAQ. It explains rules; it does not choose or submit your action.

These tools do not submit a gameplay action. After a tool returns, inspect its result and follow up wherever uncertainty remains. Use multiple calls when they test different targets, threats, rules, or memories. Treat tool results as evidence and revise your plan when they contradict an assumption. You are not limited to one tool call.

Explore as deeply as the decision warrants. Tool calls return evidence to this same run, so inspect each result and continue exploring when useful. When ready, you MUST call submit_action with arguments matching its current schema. That tool is the only way to submit the action and finish this decision. The harness checks it against the current game state before sending it to the server.

decisionJournal: Round 1 place-orders: Priorities: Capture The Reach castle (or Crackclaw Point) using a starred March from Kingswood to secure a new castle area. Use a regular Consolidate Power at Shipbreaker Bay to gain an extra power token for future bidding. Assign a regular March at Dragonstone for flexibility to move the knight or footman later, possibly to reinforce The Reach or capture another target. Preserve control of key territories and stay within the single starred order limit.

Round 1 resolve-single-march: Moved footman from Dragonstone to capture Crackclaw Point, gaining a second castle while keeping the knight at Dragonstone. No power token needed. Next focus on resolving Kingswood march to secure The Reach or reinforce positions.

Round 1 resolve-single-march: Moved footman from Kingswood to The Reach, capturing a Castle (new Baratheon castle area). Used one power token to keep control of Kingswood after vacating. Follow-up: consolidate power at Shipbreaker Bay for extra power, and monitor Lannister and Stark actions.

Round 2 bidding: Bid 2 power tokens to help the Night's Watch meet the wildling strength while preserving most of our power for future bidding and mustering. This balances defense against the wildlings with maintaining resources for upcoming influence bids and expansion.

Round 2 place-orders: Capture Kings Landing castle using footman from The Reach (starred March for +1 combat). Support from Crackclaw Point to increase combat strength. Move knight from Dragonstone to Kingswood via ship transport for future staging. Consolidate Power at Shipbreaker Bay for extra power token for upcoming bids.

Round 2 resolve-single-march: Moved the knight from Dragonstone to Kingswood to position forces adjacent to Kings Landing without sacrificing the starred March at The Reach, preserving our castle at The Reach (will leave a power token later) and setting up a future attack on Kings Landing using the upcoming starred March order. Explore liberally before deciding. Use the tools whenever they can test a route, target, threat, rule, memory, or assumption. Do not avoid a useful tool call merely to save tokens. The available tools have these purposes:

check_neighbours looks up an area's direct neighbours and their current owners, units, wounds, orders, terrain and castles. Ask about the battlefield when checking possible support. Direct neighbours are not the same as all legal ship-transport destinations.

reachable_areas finds geographic movement routes from any area, even empty or enemy-held, using your current ships for transport. It returns routes and transport ships, not legal unit groups. Armies, orders, Supply, combat strength and port control do not filter the results; use actionGuidance for legality.

inspect_house_card returns the exact printed strength, combat icons and ability text for one House card in this game, plus whether it is currently available. Use it when card text could change a combat calculation.

recall_game_state retrieves an earlier observation from your private game history. Use it when a past decision matters; the current observation takes precedence if facts differ.

remember_strategy records a proposed update to your private plan. It does not place orders or move units, and the note is saved only after your final action is accepted.

ask_rules_oracle asks a rules specialist a focused question using the local rulebook and FAQ. It explains rules; it does not choose or submit your action.

These tools do not submit a gameplay action. After a tool returns, inspect its result and follow up wherever uncertainty remains. Use multiple calls when they test different targets, threats, rules, or memories. Treat tool results as evidence and revise your plan when they contradict an assumption. You are not limited to one tool call.

Explore as deeply as the decision warrants. Tool calls return evidence to this same run, so inspect each result and continue exploring when useful. When ready, you MUST call submit_action with arguments matching its current schema. That tool is the only way to submit the action and finish this decision. The harness checks it against the current game state before sending it to the server.

decisionJournal: Round 1 place-orders: Priorities: Capture The Reach castle (or Crackclaw Point) using a starred March from Kingswood to secure a new castle area. Use a regular Consolidate Power at Shipbreaker Bay to gain an extra power token for future bidding. Assign a regular March at Dragonstone for flexibility to move the knight or footman later, possibly to reinforce The Reach or capture another target. Preserve control of key territories and stay within the single starred order limit.

Round 1 resolve-single-march: Moved footman from Dragonstone to capture Crackclaw Point, gaining a second castle while keeping the knight at Dragonstone. No power token needed. Next focus on resolving Kingswood march to secure The Reach or reinforce positions.

Round 1 resolve-single-march: Moved footman from Kingswood to The Reach, capturing a Castle (new Baratheon castle area). Used one power token to keep control of Kingswood after vacating. Follow-up: consolidate power at Shipbreaker Bay for extra power, and monitor Lannister and Stark actions.

Round 2 bidding: Bid 2 power tokens to help the Night's Watch meet the wildling strength while preserving most of our power for future bidding and mustering. This balances defense against the wildlings with maintaining resources for upcoming influence bids and expansion.

Round 2 place-orders: Capture Kings Landing castle using footman from The Reach (starred March for +1 combat). Support from Crackclaw Point to increase combat strength. Move knight from Dragonstone to Kingswood via ship transport for future staging. Consolidate Power at Shipbreaker Bay for extra power token for upcoming bids.

Round 2 resolve-single-march: Moved the knight from Dragonstone to Kingswood to position forces adjacent to Kings Landing without sacrificing the starred March at The Reach, preserving our castle at The Reach (will leave a power token later) and setting up a future attack on Kings Landing using the upcoming starred March order. This maintains supply compliance and keeps our castle count while advancing towards a stronghold capture.
Round 2 resolve-single-march: Capture Blackwater to gain 2 supply icons, increase supply track, and retain control of The Reach castle with a power token.

Round 3 place-orders: Goal: capture Lannister's Harrenhal castle this round. Use a starred March +1 from Blackwater to attack Harrenhal, supported by a regular Support order at Crackclaw Point. Keep the Knight at Kingswood safe with a Defense order. Gain an extra Power token by Consolidate Power at Shipbreaker Bay. This plan expands our castle count while maintaining supply and securing resources for future bidding.
Round 3 resolve-single-march: Capture Harrenhal castle using footman from Blackwater, supported by Crackclaw Point; spend a power token to retain Blackwater supply; keep Kingswood defended.

Round 3 choose-house-card: Play Stannis Baratheon (strength 4) to ensure victory at Harrenhal. Our base combat strength (3) plus Stannis gives 7 vs Lannister defender (3) plus any card; even if defender ties, we win tie on Fiefdoms. No sword icons needed, so no casualties are required; defender will retreat. This secures a stronghold, increasing our castle count toward victory. Valyrian Blade not owned, so not used.

We will use the 6 mustering points from our 4 castles (the‑reach, crackclaw‑point, harrenhal) and stronghold (dragonstone) to add new units: footmen at each castle and a ship at shipbreaker‑bay (or port‑of‑dragonstone) to strengthen our forces and gain ports for future power. This stays within our current supply limit and improves both offensive and defensive options.

Explore liberally before deciding. Use the tools whenever they can test a route, target, threat, rule, memory, or assumption. Do not avoid a useful tool call merely to save tokens. The available tools have these purposes:

check_neighbours looks up an area's direct neighbours and their current owners, units, wounds, orders, terrain and castles. Ask about the battlefield when checking possible support. Direct neighbours are not the same as all legal ship-transport destinations.

reachable_areas finds geographic movement routes from any area, even empty or enemy-held, using your current ships for transport. It returns routes and transport ships, not legal unit groups. Armies, orders, Supply, combat strength and port control do not filter the results; use actionGuidance for legality.

inspect_house_card returns the exact printed strength, combat icons and ability text for one House card in this game, plus whether it is currently available. Use it when card text could change a combat calculation.

recall_game_state retrieves an earlier observation from your private game history. Use it when a past decision matters; the current observation takes precedence if facts differ.

remember_strategy records a proposed update to your private plan. It does not place orders or move units, and the note is saved only after your final action is accepted.

ask_rules_oracle asks a rules specialist a focused question using the local rulebook and FAQ. It explains rules; it does not choose or submit your action.

These tools do not submit a gameplay action. After a tool returns, inspect its result and follow up wherever uncertainty remains. Use multiple calls when they test different targets, threats, rules, or memories. Treat tool results as evidence and revise your plan when they contradict an assumption. You are not limited to one tool call.

Explore as deeply as the decision warrants. Tool calls return evidence to this same run, so inspect each result and continue exploring when useful. When ready, you MUST call submit_action with arguments matching its current schema. That tool is the only way to submit the action and finish this decision. The harness checks it against the current game state before sending it to the server.

strategicMemory.situationAssessment: Round 4, phase simple-choice: baratheon controls 4 castle regions and 6 land areas, with 2 power tokens and supply 2.
objectives: Reach the castle victory threshold before all opponents.
Protect controlled castles while expanding toward the nearest attainable one.
Keep armies supply-compatible and preserve decisive house cards.
opponentModels: lannister: 4 castles, 5 land areas, 1 power tokens
stark: 2 castles, 3 land areas, 5 power tokens
decisionJournal: Round 1 place-orders: Priorities: Capture The Reach castle (or Crackclaw Point) using a starred March from Kingswood to secure a new castle area. Use a regular Consolidate Power at Shipbreaker Bay to gain an extra power token for future bidding. Assign a regular March at Dragonstone for flexibility to move the knight or footman later, possibly to reinforce The Reach or capture another target. Preserve control of key territories and stay within the single starred order limit.

Round 1 resolve-single-march: Moved footman from Dragonstone to capture Crackclaw Point, gaining a second castle while keeping the knight at Dragonstone. No power token needed. Next focus on resolving Kingswood march to secure The Reach or reinforce positions.

Round 1 resolve-single-march: Moved footman from Kingswood to The Reach, capturing a Castle (new Baratheon castle area). Used one power token to keep control of Kingswood after vacating. Follow-up: consolidate power at Shipbreaker Bay for extra power, and monitor Lannister and Stark actions.

Round 2 bidding: Bid 2 power tokens to help the Night's Watch meet the wildling strength while preserving most of our power for future bidding and mustering. This balances defense against the wildlings with maintaining resources for upcoming influence bids and expansion.

Round 2 place-orders: Capture Kings Landing castle using footman from The Reach (starred March for +1 combat). Support from Crackclaw Point to increase combat strength. Move knight from Dragonstone to Kingswood via ship transport for future staging. Consolidate Power at Shipbreaker Bay for extra power token for upcoming bids.

Round 2 resolve-single-march: Moved the knight from Dragonstone to Kingswood to position forces adjacent to Kings Landing without sacrificing the starred March at The Reach, preserving our castle at The Reach (will leave a power token later) and setting up a future attack on Kings Landing using the upcoming starred March order. This maintains supply compliance and keeps our castle count while advancing towards a stronghold capture.
Round 2 resolve-single-march: Capture Blackwater to gain 2 supply icons, increase supply track, and retain control of The Reach castle with a power token.

Round 3 place-orders: Goal: capture Lannister's Harrenhal castle this round. Use a starred March +1 from Blackwater to attack Harrenhal, supported by a regular Support order at Crackclaw Point. Keep the Knight at Kingswood safe with a Defense order. Gain an extra Power token by Consolidate Power at Shipbreaker Bay. This plan expands our castle count while maintaining supply and securing resources for future bidding.
Round 3 resolve-single-march: Capture Harrenhal castle using footman from Blackwater, supported by Crackclaw Point; spend a power token to retain Blackwater supply; keep Kingswood defended.

Round 3 choose-house-card: Play Stannis Baratheon (strength 4) to ensure victory at Harrenhal. Our base combat strength (3) plus Stannis gives 7 vs Lannister defender (3) plus any card; even if defender ties, we win tie on Fiefdoms. No sword icons needed, so no casualties are required; defender will retreat. This secures a stronghold, increasing our castle count toward victory. Valyrian Blade not owned, so not used.

Round 4 simple-choice: Choose Mustering. We will use the 6 mustering points from our 4 castles (the‑reach, crackclaw‑point, harrenhal) and stronghold (dragonstone) to add new units: footmen at each castle and a ship at shipbreaker‑bay (or port‑of‑dragonstone) to strengthen our forces and gain ports for future power. This stays within our current supply limit and improves both offensive and defensive options.

observation.decisionBriefing:
You are playing House Baratheon in round 4. This is a new decision; you have not submitted an action for it.

muster_units: You are recruiting units at the eligible mustering areas. Spend their mustering points on new pieces or Footman upgrades, using available pieces and legal destinations. The resulting armies must fit your current Supply. Upgrading a Footman replaces it with the chosen unit and does not increase that army's number of units.

skip_mustering: Decline this mustering opportunity and recruit no units.

Explore liberally before deciding. Use the tools whenever they can test a route, target, threat, rule, memory, or assumption. Do not avoid a useful tool call merely to save tokens. The available tools have these purposes:

check_neighbours looks up an area's direct neighbours and their current owners, units, wounds, orders, terrain and castles. Ask about the battlefield when checking possible support. Direct neighbours are not the same as all legal ship-transport destinations.

reachable_areas finds geographic movement routes from any area, even empty or enemy-held, using your current ships for transport. It returns routes and transport ships, not legal unit groups. Armies, orders, Supply, combat strength and port control do not filter the results; use actionGuidance for legality.

inspect_house_card returns the exact printed strength, combat icons and ability text for one House card in this game, plus whether it is currently available. Use it when card text could change a combat calculation.

recall_game_state retrieves an earlier observation from your private game history. Use it when a past decision matters; the current observation takes precedence if facts differ.

remember_strategy records a proposed update to your private plan. It does not place orders or move units, and the note is saved only after your final action is accepted.

ask_rules_oracle asks a rules specialist a focused question using the local rulebook and FAQ. It explains rules; it does not choose or submit your action.

These tools do not submit a gameplay action. After a tool returns, inspect its result and follow up wherever uncertainty remains. Use multiple calls when they test different targets, threats, rules, or memories. Treat tool results as evidence and revise your plan when they contradict an assumption. You are not limited to one tool call.

Explore as deeply as the decision warrants. Tool calls return evidence to this same run, so inspect each result and continue exploring when useful. When ready, you MUST call submit_action with arguments matching its current schema. That tool is the only way to submit the action and finish this decision. The harness checks it against the current game state before sending it to the server.

expected_schema.description: You are resolving one of your March orders. You choose which remaining March area to resolve now. Choose which units move and their destinations. Units you omit remain in the source area; you may split an army across destinations, and a single unit can march on its own. An empty moves list removes this March order without moving anyone. Only one destination may start combat. Use the reachable destinations in actionGuidance and keep the resulting armies within Supply. Leaving a control token costs one available power token and preserves control of the source when you legally vacate it. Compare castles gained and lost, and count support around the destination battlefield before choosing an attack. submit_action resolves this one order; another remaining order is a later decision.

decisionJournal: Round 2 bidding: Bid 2 power tokens to help the Night's Watch meet the wildling strength while preserving most of our power for future bidding and mustering. This balances defense against the wildlings with maintaining resources for upcoming influence bids and expansion.

Round 2 place-orders: Capture Kings Landing castle using footman from The Reach (starred March for +1 combat). Support from Crackclaw Point to increase combat strength. Move knight from Dragonstone to Kingswood via ship transport for future staging. Consolidate Power at Shipbreaker Bay for extra power token for upcoming bids.

Round 2 resolve-single-march: Moved the knight from Dragonstone to Kingswood to position forces adjacent to Kings Landing without sacrificing the starred March at The Reach, preserving our castle at The Reach (will leave a power token later) and setting up a future attack on Kings Landing using the upcoming starred March order. This maintains supply compliance and keeps our castle count while advancing towards a stronghold capture.
Round 2 resolve-single-march: Capture Blackwater to gain 2 supply icons, increase supply track, and retain control of The Reach castle with a power token.

Round 3 place-orders: Goal: capture Lannister's Harrenhal castle this round. Use a starred March +1 from Blackwater to attack Harrenhal, supported by a regular Support order at Crackclaw Point. Keep the Knight at Kingswood safe with a Defense order. Gain an extra Power token by Consolidate Power at Shipbreaker Bay. This plan expands our castle count while maintaining supply and securing resources for future bidding.
Round 3 resolve-single-march: Capture Harrenhal castle using footman from Blackwater, supported by Crackclaw Point; spend a power token to retain Blackwater supply; keep Kingswood defended.

Round 3 choose-house-card: Play Stannis Baratheon (strength 4) to ensure victory at Harrenhal. Our base combat strength (3) plus Stannis gives 7 vs Lannister defender (3) plus any card; even if defender ties, we win tie on Fiefdoms. No sword icons needed, so no casualties are required; defender will retreat. This secures a stronghold, increasing our castle count toward victory. Valyrian Blade not owned, so not used.

Round 4 simple-choice: Choose Mustering. We will use the 6 mustering points from our 4 castles (the‑reach, crackclaw‑point, harrenhal) and stronghold (dragonstone) to add new units: footmen at each castle and a ship at shipbreaker‑bay (or port‑of‑dragonstone) to strengthen our forces and gain ports for future power. This stays within our current supply limit and improves both offensive and defensive options.

Round 4 player-mustering: Muster footmen and upgrade existing footmen to knights, adding a ship at port-of-dragonstone to boost naval power while staying within supply limits, preserving power tokens for upcoming influence bids.

Round 4 bidding: Bid 2 power tokens to contribute to Night Watch defence while preserving the majority of our power (4 remaining) for upcoming Influence track bids. This moderate bid should help meet the wildling strength, which is unlikely to exceed the combined bids of all houses, and avoids excessive loss of resources that could hinder future expansions.

Round 4 place-orders: Aim to capture Kings Landing castle next round by marching the knight from Kingswood into the empty stronghold. Support the attack with a regular support order from The Reach and a starred support at Crackclaw Point to boost future combats. Defend our existing castles at Harrenhal and Dragonstone, and collect power at Shipbreaker Bay. The port at Dragonstone holds a defense order to retain control.

Round 4 resolve-single-march: March the knight from Kingswood into Kings Landing to capture the stronghold, using support from Crackclaw Point and The Reach. No control token needed; Kingswood will be vacated, gaining a castle area and improving victory position.

check_neighbours looks up an area's direct neighbours and their current owners, units, wounds, orders, terrain and castles. Ask about the battlefield when checking possible support. Direct neighbours are not the same as all legal ship-transport destinations.

decisionJournal: Round 3 resolve-single-march: Capture Harrenhal castle using footman from Blackwater, supported by Crackclaw Point; spend a power token to retain Blackwater supply; keep Kingswood defended.

Round 3 choose-house-card: Play Stannis Baratheon (strength 4) to ensure victory at Harrenhal. Our base combat strength (3) plus Stannis gives 7 vs Lannister defender (3) plus any card; even if defender ties, we win tie on Fiefdoms. No sword icons needed, so no casualties are required; defender will retreat. This secures a stronghold, increasing our castle count toward victory. Valyrian Blade not owned, so not used.

Round 4 simple-choice: Choose Mustering. We will use the 6 mustering points from our 4 castles (the‑reach, crackclaw‑point, harrenhal) and stronghold (dragonstone) to add new units: footmen at each castle and a ship at shipbreaker‑bay (or port‑of‑dragonstone) to strengthen our forces and gain ports for future power. This stays within our current supply limit and improves both offensive and defensive options.

Round 4 player-mustering: Muster footmen and upgrade existing footmen to knights, adding a ship at port-of-dragonstone to boost naval power while staying within supply limits, preserving power tokens for upcoming influence bids.

Round 4 bidding: Bid 2 power tokens to contribute to Night Watch defence while preserving the majority of our power (4 remaining) for upcoming Influence track bids. This moderate bid should help meet the wildling strength, which is unlikely to exceed the combined bids of all houses, and avoids excessive loss of resources that could hinder future expansions.

Round 4 place-orders: Aim to capture Kings Landing castle next round by marching the knight from Kingswood into the empty stronghold. Support the attack with a regular support order from The Reach and a starred support at Crackclaw Point to boost future combats. Defend our existing castles at Harrenhal and Dragonstone, and collect power at Shipbreaker Bay. The port at Dragonstone holds a defense order to retain control.

Round 4 resolve-single-march: March the knight from Kingswood into Kings Landing to capture the stronghold, using support from Crackclaw Point and The Reach. No control token needed; Kingswood will be vacated, gaining a castle area and improving victory position.

Round 5 bidding: Bid 0 power tokens to conserve resources while retaining Iron Throne position (we already hold the token) and aim to win Fiefdoms and King's Court tracks via tie-breaking. Preserving power for future bids and actions.

Round 5 resolve-ties: We keep the Iron Throne token in first position by ranking ourselves highest, then place Lannister ahead of Stark to preserve a favorable turn order for upcoming actions. This ordering conserves power for future influence bids while we continue expanding toward additional castles and securing supply. Maintaining our current lead on the Iron Throne track is critical for tie‑breaks and action sequencing.

Round 5 bidding: Bid 0 to conserve power tokens while relying on Iron Throne tie-breaking to secure first place on Fiefdoms track (Valyrian Steel Blade). Preserve power for future influence bids and actions.

Round 5 resolve-ties: Prioritize gaining the Valyrian Steel Blade by moving to first on the Fiefdoms track. Rank Baratheon first, then Lannister, then Stark to secure the Blade and improve combat tie‑breaks while preserving power for future bids.

decisionJournal: Round 4 player-mustering: Skip mustering to preserve power tokens for upcoming bidding and maintain supply. Current holdings are stable; we'll focus on planning orders next phase.

Round 4 bidding: Bid all 4 power tokens to contribute maximally to Night's Watch defense and avoid lowest-bid penalty. Preserve remaining power for upcoming influence bidding; expect opponents to have more tokens, but a full bid maximizes chance of winning or at least strong contribution.

Round 4 place-orders: Goal: expand castle count by attacking Baratheon's knight at Harrenhal from Riverrun with a starred March +1, securing the castle if successful. Protect our knight at Lannisport with a starred Defense +2 to guard against counter‑attack. Place a starred Support +1 at The Golden Sound to boost any naval combat or future ship‑based attacks. Keep a normal Defense at Moat Cailin to hold the footman while preserving our power token there. Starred orders limited to three; assignments respect that limit.

Round 4 replace-order: We keep our current orders: Defense+2 starred at Lannisport, Defense+1 at Moat Cailin, March+1 at Riverrun, Support+1 starred at The Golden Sound. No order replacement needed; preserving defenses and support is optimal this turn.

Round 4 resolve-single-march: Discard the March order from Riverrun to preserve the footman and our stronghold at Riverrun. No attack is viable (Harrenhal defended heavily). Keeping the footman maintains our castle count. No power token available to leave a control token, so moving would lose Riverrun. Therefore we empty the moves list, discarding the order.

Round 5 place-orders: Goal: expand our castle count by attacking Baratheon's stronghold at Harrenhal from Riverrun if possible, while protecting key holdings. Assign a March (non‑starred) at Riverrun to allow a footman move into Harlen. Star a Defense order at Lannisport to guard our home castle and knight. Star a Support order at The Golden Sound to boost any naval combat involving our ship. Place a normal Defense at Moat Cailin to hold that castle. This uses the two allowed starred orders (no starred March) and positions us for potential expansion while shoring up defenses.

Round 5 resolve-single-march: Discard the March order from Riverrun, keeping the footman in place to retain control via existing power token. Attacking Harrenhal would be unfavorable given Baratheon's defense +2 order and knight. No movement preserves our castle count and avoids unnecessary losses.
Round 6 bidding: Bid all 3 available power tokens to avoid being lowest bidder and help Night's Watch defeat wildlings. Preserves future influence bids while contributing maximal defense this round.
Round 6 select-house-card: Discard weakest card (Cersei) as penalty from Massing on the Milkwater wildling victory; preserve higher strength cards for future combats.

Round 6 place-orders: Goal: capture Winterfell castle by marching footman from Moat Cailin (high priority). Protect our home castle Lannisport with a starred Defense+2. Boost naval potential at The Golden Sound with a starred Support+1. Secure Riverrun with a regular Defense to deter Baratheon attacks. Use starred orders within the limit of 2.

Round 6 resolve-single-march: Discard the March order at Moat Cailin. Keeping the footman preserves our castle at Moat Cailin and avoids an unfavorable combat at White Harbor or Winterfell. No power token is left because we have none available.

Explore liberally before deciding. Use the tools whenever they can test a route, target, threat, rule, memory, or assumption. Do not avoid a useful tool call merely to save tokens. The available tools have these purposes:

check_neighbours looks up an area's direct neighbours and their current owners, units, wounds, orders, terrain and castles. Ask about the battlefield when checking possible support. Direct neighbours are not the same as all legal ship-transport destinations.

reachable_areas finds geographic movement routes from any area, even empty or enemy-held, using your current ships for transport. It returns routes and transport ships, not legal unit groups. Armies, orders, Supply, combat strength and port control do not filter the results; use actionGuidance for legality.

inspect_house_card returns the exact printed strength, combat icons and ability text for one House card in this game, plus whether it is currently available. Use it when card text could change a combat calculation.

recall_game_state retrieves an earlier observation from your private game history. Use it when a past decision matters; the current observation takes precedence if facts differ.

remember_strategy records a proposed update to your private plan. It does not place orders or move units, and the note is saved only after your final action is accepted.

ask_rules_oracle asks a rules specialist a focused question using the local rulebook and FAQ. It explains rules; it does not choose or submit your action.

These tools do not submit a gameplay action. After a tool returns, inspect its result and follow up wherever uncertainty remains. Use multiple calls when they test different targets, threats, rules, or memories. Treat tool results as evidence and revise your plan when they contradict an assumption. You are not limited to one tool call.

Explore as deeply as the decision warrants. Tool calls return evidence to this same run, so inspect each result and continue exploring when useful. When ready, you MUST call submit_action with arguments matching its current schema. That tool is the only way to submit the action and finish this decision. The harness checks it against the current game state before sending it to the server.

inspect_top_wildling_card: Use this Messenger Raven opportunity to inspect the top Wildling card. This spends the decision; keeping or burying the revealed card is a subsequent decision.

Explore liberally before deciding. Use the tools whenever they can test a route, target, threat, rule, memory, or assumption. Do not avoid a useful tool call merely to save tokens. The available tools have these purposes:

check_neighbours looks up an area's direct neighbours and their current owners, units, wounds, orders, terrain and castles. Ask about the battlefield when checking possible support. Direct neighbours are not the same as all legal ship-transport destinations.

reachable_areas finds geographic movement routes from any area, even empty or enemy-held, using your current ships for transport. It returns routes and transport ships, not legal unit groups. Armies, orders, Supply, combat strength and port control do not filter the results; use actionGuidance for legality.

inspect_house_card returns the exact printed strength, combat icons and ability text for one House card in this game, plus whether it is currently available. Use it when card text could change a combat calculation.

recall_game_state retrieves an earlier observation from your private game history. Use it when a past decision matters; the current observation takes precedence if facts differ.

remember_strategy records a proposed update to your private plan. It does not place orders or move units, and the note is saved only after your final action is accepted.

ask_rules_oracle asks a rules specialist a focused question using the local rulebook and FAQ. It explains rules; it does not choose or submit your action.

These tools do not submit a gameplay action. After a tool returns, inspect its result and follow up wherever uncertainty remains. Use multiple calls when they test different targets, threats, rules, or memories. Treat tool results as evidence and revise your plan when they contradict an assumption. You are not limited to one tool call.

Explore as deeply as the decision warrants. Tool calls return evidence to this same run, so inspect each result and continue exploring when useful. When ready, you MUST call submit_action with arguments matching its current schema. That tool is the only way to submit the action and finish this decision. The harness checks it against the current game state before sending it to the server.

check_neighbours looks up an area's direct neighbours and their current owners, units, wounds, orders, terrain and castles. Ask about the battlefield when checking possible support. Direct neighbours are not the same as all legal ship-transport destinations.

inspect_house_card returns the exact printed strength, combat icons and ability text for one House card in this game, plus whether it is currently available. Use it when card text could change a combat calculation.

recall_game_state retrieves an earlier observation from your private game history. Use it when a past decision matters; the current observation takes precedence if facts differ.

remember_strategy records a proposed update to your private plan. It does not place orders or move units, and the note is saved only after your final action is accepted.

ask_rules_oracle asks a rules specialist a focused question using the local rulebook and FAQ. It explains rules; it does not choose or submit your action.

These tools do not submit a gameplay action. After a tool returns, inspect its result and follow up wherever uncertainty remains. Use multiple calls when they test different targets, threats, rules, or memories. Treat tool results as evidence and revise your plan when they contradict an assumption. You are not limited to one tool call.

decisionJournal: Round 4 replace-order: We keep our current orders: Defense+2 starred at Lannisport, Defense+1 at Moat Cailin, March+1 at Riverrun, Support+1 starred at The Golden Sound. No order replacement needed; preserving defenses and support is optimal this turn.

Round 4 resolve-single-march: Discard the March order from Riverrun to preserve the footman and our stronghold at Riverrun. No attack is viable (Harrenhal defended heavily). Keeping the footman maintains our castle count. No power token available to leave a control token, so moving would lose Riverrun. Therefore we empty the moves list, discarding the order.

Round 5 place-orders: Goal: expand our castle count by attacking Baratheon's stronghold at Harrenhal from Riverrun if possible, while protecting key holdings. Assign a March (non‑starred) at Riverrun to allow a footman move into Harlen. Star a Defense order at Lannisport to guard our home castle and knight. Star a Support order at The Golden Sound to boost any naval combat involving our ship. Place a normal Defense at Moat Cailin to hold that castle. This uses the two allowed starred orders (no starred March) and positions us for potential expansion while shoring up defenses.

Round 5 resolve-single-march: Discard the March order from Riverrun, keeping the footman in place to retain control via existing power token. Attacking Harrenhal would be unfavorable given Baratheon's defense +2 order and knight. No movement preserves our castle count and avoids unnecessary losses.
Round 6 bidding: Bid all 3 available power tokens to avoid being lowest bidder and help Night's Watch defeat wildlings. Preserves future influence bids while contributing maximal defense this round.
Round 6 select-house-card: Discard weakest card (Cersei) as penalty from Massing on the Milkwater wildling victory; preserve higher strength cards for future combats.

Round 6 place-orders: Goal: capture Winterfell castle by marching footman from Moat Cailin (high priority). Protect our home castle Lannisport with a starred Defense+2. Boost naval potential at The Golden Sound with a starred Support+1. Secure Riverrun with a regular Defense to deter Baratheon attacks. Use starred orders within the limit of 2.

Round 6 resolve-single-march: Discard the March order at Moat Cailin. Keeping the footman preserves our castle at Moat Cailin and avoids an unfavorable combat at White Harbor or Winterfell. No power token is left because we have none available.

Round 6 choose-house-card: Combat at White Harbor vs Moat Cailin: Lannister defender has 1 footman (strength1). To secure win, play strongest card Ser Gregor Clegane (strength3, 3 swords). Baron Baratheon holds Valyrian Blade, not usable. This ensures Lannister victory and eliminates Stark footmen.
Round 7 player-mustering: We skip mustering this turn to conserve resources, maintain supply balance, and keep focus on upcoming combat and bidding. No new units are recruited.

Round 7 place-orders: Goal: capture White Harbor castle using a starred March from Moat Cailin, gain a power token at Riverrun via Consolidate Power, keep naval support at The Golden Sound (starred) and provide ground support from Lannisport. Preserve our existing castles and increase victory points.

muster_units: You are recruiting units at the eligible mustering areas. Spend their mustering points on new pieces or Footman upgrades, using available pieces and legal destinations. Explore liberally before deciding. Use the tools whenever they can test a route, target, threat, rule, memory, or assumption. Do not avoid a useful tool call merely to save tokens. The available tools have these purposes:

check_neighbours looks up an area's direct neighbours and their current owners, units, wounds, orders, terrain and castles. Ask about the battlefield when checking possible support. Direct neighbours are not the same as all legal ship-transport destinations.

reachable_areas finds geographic movement routes from any area, even empty or enemy-held, using your current ships for transport. It returns routes and transport ships, not legal unit groups. Armies, orders, Supply, combat strength and port control do not filter the results; use actionGuidance for legality.

inspect_house_card returns the exact printed strength, combat icons and ability text for one House card in this game, plus whether it is currently available. Use it when card text could change a combat calculation.

recall_game_state retrieves an earlier observation from your private game history. Use it when a past decision matters; the current observation takes precedence if facts differ.

remember_strategy records a proposed update to your private plan. It does not place orders or move units, and the note is saved only after your final action is accepted.

ask_rules_oracle asks a rules specialist a focused question using the local rulebook and FAQ. It explains rules; it does not choose or submit your action.

These tools do not submit a gameplay action. After a tool returns, inspect its result and follow up wherever uncertainty remains. Use multiple calls when they test different targets, threats, rules, or memories. Treat tool results as evidence and revise your plan when they contradict an assumption. You are not limited to one tool call.

Explore as deeply as the decision warrants. Tool calls return evidence to this same run, so inspect each result and continue exploring when useful. When ready, you MUST call submit_action with arguments matching its current schema. That tool is the only way to submit the action and finish this decision. The harness checks it against the current game state before sending it to the server.

decisionJournal: Round 4 bidding: Bid all 6 power tokens to ensure Night's Watch total meets or exceeds the wildling strength and to secure the reward as highest bidder. This maximizes our short-term safety against the wildling attack, preserving our castles and units, even though it exhausts our current power tokens; we will regain tokens via upcoming Consolidate Power orders and future Westeros cards.

Round 4 place-orders: Maintain our two castles (Winterfell stronghold and White Harbor castle) while reinforcing Winterfell. Use a March order from The Stony Shore to move the knight into Winterfell, strengthening our home stronghold without sacrificing control of White Harbor. Assign a Defense order to White Harbor to protect its castle. Provide a starred Support order from the ship in The Shivering Sea to boost any future combat we may initiate, giving us flexibility to attack nearby enemy holdings later. This allocation respects the two-star limit and positions us to expand toward opponent castles in upcoming rounds.

Round 4 resolve-single-march: Move the Stark knight from The Stony Shore to Winterfell, preserving our stronghold without losing any castle area and staying within supply. No power token is needed as the area has no castle, and this positions us for future actions.

Round 5 place-orders: Maintain defense of our two castles (Winterfell and White Harbor). Use a regular March order from Winterfell to move the knight toward the unoccupied Stony Shore next round, expanding our land control without risking combat. Assign a regular Defense order to White Harbor to protect its castle. Provide a starred Support order from the ship at The Shivering Sea to boost future attacks if we choose to engage nearby enemy holdings. This respects the single starred order limit and avoids starring a March order.

Round 5 resolve-single-march: Moved Stark knight from Winterfell to the Stony Shore to expand land control without combat. No power token needed as Winterfell is home area. This preserves our castle and prepares for future advances toward enemy holdings.

Round 6 bidding: Conserve our sole power token; Baratheon and Lannister have larger token pools and will likely outbid us, ensuring Night's Watch total exceeds wildling strength. Bidding 0 preserves the token for future Consolidate Power gains.

Explore liberally before deciding. Use the tools whenever they can test a route, target, threat, rule, memory, or assumption. Do not avoid a useful tool call merely to save tokens. The available tools have these purposes:

check_neighbours looks up an area's direct neighbours and their current owners, units, wounds, orders, terrain and castles. Ask about the battlefield when checking possible support. Direct neighbours are not the same as all legal ship-transport destinations.

reachable_areas finds geographic movement routes from any area, even empty or enemy-held, using your current ships for transport. It returns routes and transport ships, not legal unit groups. Armies, orders, Supply, combat strength and port control do not filter the results; use actionGuidance for legality.

inspect_house_card returns the exact printed strength, combat icons and ability text for one House card in this game, plus whether it is currently available. Use it when card text could change a combat calculation.

recall_game_state retrieves an earlier observation from your private game history. Use it when a past decision matters; the current observation takes precedence if facts differ.

remember_strategy records a proposed update to your private plan. It does not place orders or move units, and the note is saved only after your final action is accepted.

ask_rules_oracle asks a rules specialist a focused question using the local rulebook and FAQ. It explains rules; it does not choose or submit your action.

These tools do not submit a gameplay action. After a tool returns, inspect its result and follow up wherever uncertainty remains. Use multiple calls when they test different targets, threats, rules, or memories. Treat tool results as evidence and revise your plan when they contradict an assumption. You are not limited to one tool call.

Explore as deeply as the decision warrants. Tool calls return evidence to this same run, so inspect each result and continue exploring when useful. When ready, you MUST call submit_action with arguments matching its current schema. That tool is the only way to submit the action and finish this decision. The harness checks it against the current game state before sending it to the server.

check_neighbours looks up an area's direct neighbours and their current owners, units, wounds, orders, terrain and castles. Ask about the battlefield when checking possible support. Direct neighbours are not the same as all legal ship-transport destinations.

reachable_areas finds geographic movement routes from any area, even empty or enemy-held, using your current ships for transport. It returns routes and transport ships, not legal unit groups. inspect_house_card returns the exact printed strength, combat icons and ability text for one House card in this game, plus whether it is currently available. Use it when card text could change a combat calculation.

recall_game_state retrieves an earlier observation from your private game history. Use it when a past decision matters; the current observation takes precedence if facts differ.

remember_strategy records a proposed update to your private plan. It does not place orders or move units, and the note is saved only after your final action is accepted.

ask_rules_oracle asks a rules specialist a focused question using the local rulebook and FAQ. It explains rules; it does not choose or submit your action.

These tools do not submit a gameplay action. After a tool returns, inspect its result and follow up wherever uncertainty remains. Use multiple calls when they test different targets, threats, rules, or memories. Treat tool results as evidence and revise your plan when they contradict an assumption. check_neighbours looks up an area's direct neighbours and their current owners, units, wounds, orders, terrain and castles. Ask about the battlefield when checking possible support. Direct neighbours are not the same as all legal ship-transport destinations.

reachable_areas finds geographic movement routes from any area, even empty or enemy-held, using your current ships for transport. It returns routes and transport ships, not legal unit groups. inspect_house_card returns the exact printed strength, combat icons and ability text for one House card in this game, plus whether it is currently available. Use it when card text could change a combat calculation.

recall_game_state retrieves an earlier observation from your private game history. Use it when a past decision matters; the current observation takes precedence if facts differ.

remember_strategy records a proposed update to your private plan. It does not place orders or move units, and the note is saved only after your final action is accepted.

ask_rules_oracle asks a rules specialist a focused question using the local rulebook and FAQ. It explains rules; it does not choose or submit your action.

These tools do not submit a gameplay action. After a tool returns, inspect its result and follow up wherever uncertainty remains. Use multiple calls when they test different targets, threats, rules, or memories. Treat tool results as evidence and revise your plan when they contradict an assumption. check_neighbours looks up an area's direct neighbours and their current owners, units, wounds, orders, terrain and castles. Ask about the battlefield when checking possible support. Direct neighbours are not the same as all legal ship-transport destinations.

reachable_areas finds geographic movement routes from any area, even empty or enemy-held, using your current ships for transport. It returns routes and transport ships, not legal unit groups. recall_game_state retrieves an earlier observation from your private game history. Use it when a past decision matters; the current observation takes precedence if facts differ.

remember_strategy records a proposed update to your private plan. It does not place orders or move units, and the note is saved only after your final action is accepted.

ask_rules_oracle asks a rules specialist a focused question using the local rulebook and FAQ. It explains rules; it does not choose or submit your action.

These tools do not submit a gameplay action. After a tool returns, inspect its result and follow up wherever uncertainty remains. Use multiple calls when they test different targets, threats, rules, or memories. Treat tool results as evidence and revise your plan when they contradict an assumption. You are not limited to one tool call.

Explore as deeply as the decision warrants. Tool calls return evidence to this same run, so inspect each result and continue exploring when useful. Explore liberally before deciding. Use the tools whenever they can test a route, target, threat, rule, memory, or assumption. Do not avoid a useful tool call merely to save tokens. The available tools have these purposes:

check_neighbours looks up an area's direct neighbours and their current owners, units, wounds, orders, terrain and castles. Ask about the battlefield when checking possible support. Direct neighbours are not the same as all legal ship-transport destinations.

reachable_areas finds geographic movement routes from any area, even empty or enemy-held, using your current ships for transport. It returns routes and transport ships, not legal unit groups. Armies, orders, Supply, combat strength and port control do not filter the results; use actionGuidance for legality.

inspect_house_card returns the exact printed strength, combat icons and ability text for one House card in this game, plus whether it is currently available. Use it when card text could change a combat calculation.

recall_game_state retrieves an earlier observation from your private game history. Use it when a past decision matters; the current observation takes precedence if facts differ.

remember_strategy records a proposed update to your private plan. It does not place orders or move units, and the note is saved only after your final action is accepted.

ask_rules_oracle asks a rules specialist a focused question using the local rulebook and FAQ. It explains rules; it does not choose or submit your action.

These tools do not submit a gameplay action. After a tool returns, inspect its result and follow up wherever uncertainty remains. Use multiple calls when they test different targets, threats, rules, or memories. Treat tool results as evidence and revise your plan when they contradict an assumption. You are not limited to one tool call.

Explore as deeply as the decision warrants. Tool calls return evidence to this same run, so inspect each result and continue exploring when useful. When ready, you MUST call submit_action with arguments matching its current schema. That tool is the only way to submit the action and finish this decision. The harness checks it against the current game state before sending it to the server.

Explore liberally before deciding. Use the tools whenever they can test a route, target, threat, rule, memory, or assumption. Do not avoid a useful tool call merely to save tokens. The available tools have these purposes:

check_neighbours looks up an area's direct neighbours and their current owners, units, wounds, orders, terrain and castles. Ask about the battlefield when checking possible support. Direct neighbours are not the same as all legal ship-transport destinations.

reachable_areas finds geographic movement routes from any area, even empty or enemy-held, using your current ships for transport. It returns routes and transport ships, not legal unit groups. Armies, orders, Supply, combat strength and port control do not filter the results; use actionGuidance for legality.

inspect_house_card returns the exact printed strength, combat icons and ability text for one House card in this game, plus whether it is currently available. Use it when card text could change a combat calculation.

recall_game_state retrieves an earlier observation from your private game history. Use it when a past decision matters; the current observation takes precedence if facts differ.

remember_strategy records a proposed update to your private plan. It does not place orders or move units, and the note is saved only after your final action is accepted.

ask_rules_oracle asks a rules specialist a focused question using the local rulebook and FAQ. It explains rules; it does not choose or submit your action.

These tools do not submit a gameplay action. After a tool returns, inspect its result and follow up wherever uncertainty remains. Use multiple calls when they test different targets, threats, rules, or memories. Treat tool results as evidence and revise your plan when they contradict an assumption. You are not limited to one tool call.

Explore as deeply as the decision warrants. Tool calls return evidence to this same run, so inspect each result and continue exploring when useful. Explore liberally before deciding. Use the tools whenever they can test a route, target, threat, rule, memory, or assumption. Do not avoid a useful tool call merely to save tokens. The available tools have these purposes:

check_neighbours looks up an area's direct neighbours and their current owners, units, wounds, orders, terrain and castles. Ask about the battlefield when checking possible support. Direct neighbours are not the same as all legal ship-transport destinations.

reachable_areas finds geographic movement routes from any area, even empty or enemy-held, using your current ships for transport. It returns routes and transport ships, not legal unit groups. inspect_house_card returns the exact printed strength, combat icons and ability text for one House card in this game, plus whether it is currently available. Use it when card text could change a combat calculation.

recall_game_state retrieves an earlier observation from your private game history. Use it when a past decision matters; the current observation takes precedence if facts differ.

remember_strategy records a proposed update to your private plan. It does not place orders or move units, and the note is saved only after your final action is accepted.

ask_rules_oracle asks a rules specialist a focused question using the local rulebook and FAQ. It explains rules; it does not choose or submit your action.

These tools do not submit a gameplay action. After a tool returns, inspect its result and follow up wherever uncertainty remains. Use multiple calls when they test different targets, threats, rules, or memories. Treat tool results as evidence and revise your plan when they contradict an assumption. You are not limited to one tool call.

Explore as deeply as the decision warrants. Tool calls return evidence to this same run, so inspect each result and continue exploring when useful. When ready, you MUST call submit_action with arguments matching its current schema. That tool is the only way to submit the action and finish this decision.
